Uganda Electric Utilities Strike Disrupts Grid Operations

A nationwide walkout by workers in Uganda’s electric utilities sector entered its second day on Thursday, leaving transmission and distribution operations hampered across much of the country. The industrial action, which began on Wednesday morning, has affected Uganda Electricity Transmission Co Ltd and several other key players in the sector.

According to the Uganda Energy Workers Union, the strike was called after protracted negotiations on wage increments and improved working conditions broke down last week. “Our members have been patient for too long. We are demanding fair pay and safer working environments,” said union secretary Peter Mugisha. 

Sources at Uganda Electricity Transmission Co Ltd confirmed that routine maintenance and emergency repair work have been severely affected, with some scheduled upgrades postponed indefinitely. “We are doing everything possible to keep the grid stable, but the absence of our technical teams is having a real impact,” a company spokesperson said.

Industry analysts estimate that transmission capacity has been reduced by up to 40 percent nationwide, with load-shedding measures implemented to balance supply. Florence Katusabe, an energy market consultant based in Kampala, commented: “Continued disruption at this scale could have long-term implications for grid reliability and future investment in the sector.”

The Uganda Electric Utilities Association, representing several sector operators, has urged all parties to return to the negotiating table. “The industry cannot function without its skilled workforce. We hope for a swift and amicable resolution,” the association said in a statement.

At the time of writing, talks between union representatives and utility management had not resumed. Workers have vowed to continue the walkout until their demands are addressed, raising concerns about prolonged operational disruptions in Uganda’s electric utilities industry.
